# `silk/git/pkt_line`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read and write pkt-lines, the length-prefixed framing of the Git wire protocol.

## When to use
Use [`PktLine.read`](#PktLine.impl.read) to walk the packets of a Git protocol message, such as the body of a
`git-upload-pack` response, and [`PktLine.appendData`](#PktLine.impl.appendData) with [`PktLine.appendFlush`](#PktLine.impl.appendFlush) and
[`PktLine.appendDelimiter`](#PktLine.impl.appendDelimiter) to build a request body. Most programs use `silk.git.remote`, which
does this for you.

## Details
Each packet starts with four hexadecimal digits that give its length, the four digits included.
`0000` is a flush packet, `0001` a delimiter, and `0002` a response end. A longer length is a
data packet of at most 65516 payload bytes. [`PktLine.read`](#PktLine.impl.read) returns a [`Packet`](#Packet) of offsets
into the input, so nothing is copied. [`PktLine.line`](#PktLine.impl.line) returns the payload without its final
LF, the form in which most Git text lines are sent.

## Errors
- [`PktLineError`](#PktLineError) for a length that is not four hexadecimal digits, is 3, or runs past the
  input, and for a payload that is too long to write.
- `OutOfMemoryError` from the append functions.

## Examples
### Write two packets and read them back
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.collections.bytes { Bytes }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.git.pkt_line { Packet, PacketKind, PktLine, PktLineError }

effect fn roundTrip() -> bool ! PktLineError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let mut body = Bytes.make()
  run PktLine.appendData(&mut body, b"command=ls-refs\n")
  run PktLine.appendFlush(&mut body)
  let input = Bytes.asSlice(&body)
  let first = match PktLine.read(input, 0) {
    Result<Packet, PktLineError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<Packet, PktLineError>.Failure { error } => { fail move error }
  }
  let line = PktLine.line(input, &first)
  let second = match PktLine.read(input, first.next) {
    Result<Packet, PktLineError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<Packet, PktLineError>.Failure { error } => { fail move error }
  }
  let flushed = match second.kind {
    PacketKind.Flush => true
    _ => false
  }
  return line.length == 15 && flushed && second.next == input.length
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! PktLineError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  if run roundTrip() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator) {
    return 0
  }
  return 1
}
```

<a id="Packet"></a>

## `Packet`

```silk
pub struct Packet
```

One packet, as offsets into the input that [`PktLine.read`](#PktLine.impl.read) read.

### Details

The payload is from `start` to `end`, after the four length digits. A packet that is not
`Data` has an empty payload. The next packet starts at `next`.

<a id="PktLine.impl.read"></a>

### Associated function `read`

```silk
pub fn read(input: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result<Packet, PktLineError>
```

Returns the packet that starts at `offset` of `input`.

#### Details

The four length digits can be upper or lower case. Nothing is copied: the [`Packet`](#Packet) holds
offsets into `input`. Read the next packet at `packet.next`.

#### Errors

- `Truncated` if fewer than four bytes start at `offset`, or the payload runs past the end.
- `InvalidLength` if the length is not four hexadecimal digits, or it is 3.

<a id="PktLine.impl.payload"></a>

### Associated function `payload`

```silk
pub fn payload<'a>(input: &'a [u8], packet: &Packet) -> &'a [u8]
```

Returns the payload of `packet` in `input`. It is empty for a packet that is not `Data`.

<a id="PktLine.impl.line"></a>

### Associated function `line`

```silk
pub fn line<'a>(input: &'a [u8], packet: &Packet) -> &'a [u8]
```

Returns the payload of `packet` in `input` without its final LF, if it has one.

#### When to use

Use it for the text lines of the protocol, which a sender may end with LF or not.

<a id="PktLine.impl.appendData"></a>

### Associated function `appendData`

```silk
pub effect fn appendData(output: &mut Bytes, payload: &[u8]) -> ()
    ! PktLineError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends a data packet with `payload` to `output`: its four length digits in lower case, then
the payload.

#### Errors

- `PayloadTooLong` if `payload` has more than [`MAX_PAYLOAD`](#MAX_PAYLOAD) bytes. `output` does not change.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot grow `output`.
